verdict.line: You lose if you stand in Aatrox's Q/W poke range before level 6 and get chipped down before you can engage; you win if you survive to itemize and force a stacked-Hemorrhage all-in where Guillotine's true damage outpaces his healing.

brief.thesis: Aatrox has ranged pressure tools (Q's three swings, W's 825-range Infernal Chains) and self-heal (Deathbringer Stance, Umbral Dash's passive heal) that punish Darius for closing distance, which is exactly why OP.GG's tip is to dodge the Q-E poke before fighting in close quarters. Darius's own E (Apprehend, 535 range) is the counter to that pattern — it's a gap-closing pull, not just an engage tool, and it's strongest the moment Aatrox has spent E (Umbral Dash) to disengage.

theirWindow.when: Q, W, E and stance all up
theirWindow.what: Aatrox can poke with Q (The Darkin Blade) and W (Infernal Chains) then dash away with E (Umbral Dash, 9-5s cd) before you close. Don't contest CS or trade in his 825-range W threat zone during this window.

yourWindow.when: his E (Umbral Dash) just went on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Land Apprehend (E, 535 range) to pull him into melee where he can't reset with the dash. This is your best window to stack Hemorrhage and get a real trade.

start.why: The 81% pick rate, 48.3% win rate start over 205 games — the extra sustain and damage help you survive his early poke long enough to look for an E pull.

boots.why: 81.6% pick, 51.3% win rate over 199 games. Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance auto and repeated Q swings are basic attacks and physical damage — flat reduction blunts both his poke and his heal-back.

core.why: First item in the 53.8% win rate path over 26 games; the active gives you the burst of mobility to close on E-cooldown windows before he can Umbral Dash away again.
Second in that same path — the move speed lets you actually stay attached through his poke phase instead of eating it from range.
Completes the 53.8%-winrate, 20.6%-pick core; the damage mitigation matters against a champion whose kit is built to heal off you in extended fights.

situational.when: his healing and stacked AD are snowballing the fight (this swap is part of the 66.7% win rate Youmuu's/DMP/FoN path over 9 games)
you need burst survivability to actually land your all-in instead of dying to his empowered auto first
you're ahead and want to shorten Apprehend and Guillotine cooldowns to punish his dash windows more often

runes.keystoneWhy: 53.4% win rate, 23% pick — the stacking adaptive force rewards the extended fights you're forced into once you finally land Apprehend. Master-tier Darius players instead run Stormraider's Surge (Sorcery keystone, 932 games) — that suits a more hit-and-run style that leans on Celerity and Gathering Storm rather than sustained trading, worth considering if you're not confident closing distance repeatedly.

summoners.why: Flash+Ghost is both the most-played (65.9% pick) and highest-winning (50.6%) combo — the extra Ghost uptime helps you close the gap on his poke instead of eating it from range. Flash+Ignite (48.1% win rate, 31.4% pick) is the alternative if you want to secure kills against his self-healing kit.

playing.title: Hold Q for safe stacks only
playing.detail: Decimate (Q, 9-5s cd depending on rank) is your CS and Hemorrhage tool, but walking up to use it into his Q/W range just feeds his poke. Only take it when he's out of range or already engaged.

playing.title: Pull him the moment E dash is down
playing.detail: Apprehend (E, 535 range) is strongest immediately after he burns Umbral Dash to poke-and-leave. Without that dash he can't disengage your pull, so this is your real engage window, not a random level-6 all-in.

playing.title: Track the Deathbringer Stance icon
playing.detail: Never trade autos into his empowered stance — it deals bonus magic damage and heals him off your max health. Wait for him to burn it on a minion or bait it out before committing.

playing.title: Bank stacks before using R
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales with his Hemorrhage stack count, so land Q and autos to build stacks first; a 5-stack Guillotine is a completely different threat than a 1-stack one.

playing.title: Play the lane defensively through level 5
playing.detail: Both lane and solo-kill stats favor Aatrox pre-6. Don't contest 50/50 trades in his W (Infernal Chains, 825 range) threat zone — concede some CS if it keeps you out of his combo.

playing.title: Look to skirmish once Youmuu's is up
playing.detail: Your win condition arrives with the item core, not the early lane. The active haste from Youmuu's Ghostblade is what finally lets you match his mobility instead of losing every extended chase.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners and all win-rate/pick-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning about cooldown windows, stance timing and trade patterns is my own tactical read, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit by Aatrox’s (Q)-(E) combo. Avoid his pokes while closing in to fight him in close quarters.
